import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
from jobs import unique_jobs

def test_basic():
    rows = [
        {'source': 'A', 'source_id': 1, 'title': 'Job1'},
        {'source': 'A', 'source_id': 2, 'title': 'Job2'},
        {'source': 'B', 'source_id': 1, 'title': 'Job3'},
    ]
    result = unique_jobs(rows)
    assert len(result) == 3, f'expected 3, got {len(result)}'
    # order should be original order
    assert result[0] is rows[0]
    assert result[1] is rows[1]
    assert result[2] is rows[2]

def test_none_source_id():
    rows = [
        {'source': 'X', 'source_id': None, 'title': 'Job1'},
        {'source': 'X', 'source_id': '', 'title': 'Job2'},
        {'source': 'X', 'source_id': 1, 'title': 'Job3'},
    ]
    result = unique_jobs(rows)
    # None and '' should be considered same key? The spec: Missing/None/empty source_id means keep row separately.
    # Actually spec: Missing/None/empty source_id means keep the row separately.
    # Means treat each as distinct? It says keep the row separately, i.e., don't merge across sources or by title.
    # So each row should be kept if source_id missing/None/empty.
    # So we expect all three kept, order preserved.
    assert len(result) == 3

def test_duplicate_by_key():
    rows = [
        {'source': 'A', 'source_id': 1, 'title': 'Job1'},
        {'source': 'A', 'source_id': 1, 'title': 'Job1b'},  # same key, title may differ; spec merges? No merge across sources or by title; here same source and source_id, key same -> first occurrence wins.
        {'source': 'A', 'source_id': 1, 'title': 'Job1c'},
    ]
    result = unique_jobs(rows)
    assert len(result) == 1  # only first kept
    assert result[0] is rows[0]

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_basic()
    test_none_source_id()
    test_duplicate_by_key()
    print('All tests passed')
